'''Andrew Bruce Forbes Williams''' (born 1959) is a New Zealand former politician. In 2007 he won election as Mayor of [[North Shore City]]. Williams served on a community board during 2004–2007, and as a city councillor in the term before that in 2001–2004. [[North Shore City]] Council was abolished in October 2010, becoming part of the [[Auckland Council|Auckland "Super City"]]. Williams won election to the [[New Zealand Parliament]] on 26 November 2011 as a list MP for the [[New Zealand First]] Party, but only served one term.

== Political career ==

===Local Government politics===
Williams served as a North Shore City councillor between 2001 and 2004, and Takapuna community board member between 2004 and 2007. He was a Hearings Commissioner from 2001 to 2010.

In 2007 he won election as [[Mayor of North Shore City]], New Zealand's fourth-largest city at the time. North Shore City Council was abolished in October 2010, becoming part of the [[Auckland Council|Auckland "Super City"]].

Williams was an outspoken critic of the "Super City" amalgamation process for Auckland instigated by the [[Fifth National Government of New Zealand|National-led government]] in its first term of 2008–2011, considering the proposed "Supercity" unnecessary and undemocratic. He called the political moves towards forced unification a railroaded process and a power grab.<ref name="MADNESS">''[http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10571023 Andrew Williams: Downsize this Super City madness]'', ''[[The New Zealand Herald]]'', Friday 8 May 2009
</ref> Personal relations with [[Auckland City]]'s mayor [[John Banks (New Zealand politician)|John Banks]] reportedly turned sour, with Banks calling Williams "a lunatic" in a text message Banks accidentally sent to Williams, after Williams had accused [[Rodney Hide]] of misleading the Prime Minister on the amount of consultation with local authorities on the "Super City" proposal.<ref>
[http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10566362 "Banks calls Williams a lunatic as Super City debate gets ugly"], ''[[The New Zealand Herald]]'', Monday 13 April 2009</ref>

On 15 August 2008, Williams collapsed while attending a Devonport naval base function. While being treated by ambulance workers, Williams is said to have "lashed out" at those helping him. The ambulance staff filed an incident report, but did not recommend further action.<ref name="NZ_Herald_10527445">{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10527445 |title=Sick mayor and ambulance staff run-in |author=Savage, Jared |date=17 August 2008 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |accessdate=16 September 2011}}</ref> Williams' wife Jane (a registered nurse) said her husband was suffering from "Chinese lurgy" after having just arrived back from an exhausting 10-day trip to Korea and China as a guest of both those governments. She described the incident as an unconscious reaction of Williams as the medics treated him, and expressed surprise that the media had been told of it even though it should have been covered by patient confidentiality.<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_589626">{{cite news |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/north-shore-times/589626 |title=Mayoress concerned about patient confidentiality |date=20 August 2008 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |accessdate=16 September 2011}}</ref>

Local newspapers were critical of Williams' first year in the Mayor's office, with one tabloid paper asking the question "Is the mayor mad?" and noting that his behaviour was described as "overbearing, controlling, heavy-handed". Williams defended himself as not having "a lot of patience for fence-sitters and procrastinators",<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.theaucklander.co.nz/local/news/is-the-mayor-mad/3789009/ |title=Is the mayor mad? |work=[[The Aucklander]] |date=30 October 2008 |access-date=3 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724153902/http://www.theaucklander.co.nz/local/news/is-the-mayor-mad/3789009/ |archive-date=24 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and he believed this was shown to be the case by the significant results the city achieved during his three years of mayoralty.

Williams has been involved in a number of heated incidents – such as during a meeting of a committee of the North Shore City Council, where he was asked to leave after referring to a councillor, [[Chris Darby]], as a "smart-arse".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10542786 |title=Mayor defiant over council name-calling |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date= 13 November 2008}}</ref> Darby was part of a minority of councillors who constantly opposed the policies and actions by what the media called Mayor Andrew's "A Team".<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10635228 |title=Embattled mayor to make announcement on future |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

Regarding the then-proposed Super City, Williams instead called for retention of the local Councils as they existed as of 2009, with a stronger [[Auckland Regional Council]] that could allegedly be made more accountable by being made up of local authority councillors instead of being elected separately and being forced to "work in a silo", "with insufficient funding".<ref name="MADNESS" /> The position taken by Williams and the North Shore City Council was in line with the final report and recommendations of the Royal Commission on Auckland Governance.

Williams was accused of sending a late night text to North Shore-based Government MPs (as Parliament rose from a late night midnight final sitting on the Auckland Supercity Bill), including Prime Minister [[John Key]]. Williams was expressing his great disappointment of their final vote approving the SuperCity.

In July 2010, he announced that he would stand in the [[2010 Auckland mayoral election|2010 mayoral election]] for the new 'Supercity' and for the Albany ward on the new council.<ref name="SUPERMAYOR">{{cite news|title=Andrew Williams: I want to be Super Mayor|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10657858|accessdate=10 July 2010|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=10 July 2010|first=Bernard|last=Orsman}}</ref> His aim was not to win but to reduce votes for John Banks on the North Shore. He was elected to neither, and retired as the final Mayor of North Shore City after a council meeting on the last day of the city's legal existence on 31 October 2010.

===Member of Parliament (2011–2014)===

{{End}}
He represented [[New Zealand First]] in the [[North Shore (New Zealand electorate)|North Shore]] in the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 general election]].<ref name="Stuff.co.nz_5380201">{{cite web |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/5380201/Andrew-Williams-to-contest-North-Shore-seat |title=Andrew Williams to contest North Shore seat |author=Vance, Andrea |date=2 August 2011 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |accessdate=16 September 2011}}</ref> Although New Zealand First won no electorate seats, Williams was elected as a list Member of Parliament as New Zealand First's 6.8% of the party vote entitled it to eight seats in Parliament.<ref>''[http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/6041932/New-Zealand-First-back-from-wilderness-with-eight-MPs Peters back from wilderness]'', Fairfax Newspapers, 27 November 2011</ref> Williams himself only received just over 800 votes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10769275|title = He 'only got 828 votes' - Maggie Barry takes swipe at ex-mayor| date=27 November 2011 }}</ref>

On 26 August 2014, New Zealand First released their parliamentary list for the [[2014 New Zealand general election]]. Williams was excluded, effectively ending his parliamentary career.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/10425217/NZ-First-wipes-Andrew-Williams-from-list|title=NZ First wipes Andrew Williams from list|first=Hamish|last=Rutherford|date=26 August 2014|via=Stuff.co.nz}}</ref>

Following his electoral defeat, Williams and his wife retired to [[Taupō]].
